new_scholarship.name: Bourse du Gouvernement Français (French Government Scholarship)
new_scholarship.official_source: French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs (Ministère de l'Europe et des Affaires étrangères), implemented by Campus France
new_scholarship.duration: Awarded for a fixed period tied to the programme; the Licence-level rate applies for the duration of the degree.
new_scholarship.deadline: "Quel que soit leur pays de résidence, les candidats doivent donc, avant leur départ et suffisamment à l'avance, s'adresser directement à ces services [Services de coopération et d'action culturelle des ambassades et des consulats généraux] situés dans leurs pays d'origine afin d'obtenir toutes les informations sur ces bourses : conditions d'attribution, calendrier de sélection, dossiers à constituer."
new_scholarship.application_period: There is no single global application window. Each French embassy or consulate abroad sets its own selection calendar for the scholarships it awards, generally for the following academic year.
new_scholarship.application_method: Not automatic on admission. The scholarship is applied for directly to the French embassy or consulate (Service de coopération et d'action culturelle) in the candidate's country of residence; separately, admission to a French institution is applied for through the national admissions platform for the degree level (the 'Etudes en France' platform, pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr, for first-year Licence applications).
new_scholarship.description: The Bourse du Gouvernement Français is the umbrella status for French government scholarships awarded by the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs for study, internship and short research or language stays in France. Most of them are awarded by the cultural cooperation services of French embassies and consulates abroad rather than in Paris. Campus France implements the awarded scholarship and publishes the official rate grid: EUR 900 per month for a Licence (bachelor's) or Master's level scholarship and EUR 1,850 per month for a doctoral one. Holders are exempted from the CVEC student contribution and from enrolment fees for national and engineering degrees in public higher education establishments under the Minister for Higher Education, but training fees and other living costs remain with the holder.
new_scholarship.best_fit: Foreign students from a country served by a French embassy or consulate that runs a French Government Scholarship call at Licence level, who have been admitted or are applying to a French higher education programme and who accept the reporting and attendance obligations attached to scholarship-holder status.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: The award targets foreign students. It is not open to French nationals. Nationality rules, subject areas, eligible levels and selection criteria are set by the awarding embassy or consulate for each country, so eligibility is defined per country; the ministry reserves some specific programmes for particular nationality groups. Applicants must be admitted to or applying to a French higher education programme and must sign and honour the scholarship-holder obligations.
eligibility: Be a foreign (non-French) student; French nationals are not eligible
Be a national of a country served by a French embassy or consulate that awards French Government Scholarships at Licence level
Apply through the French embassy or consulate in the country of residence, which sets the nationality, level and subject conditions for its own call
Be admitted to, or apply for, a French higher education programme; the scholarship is awarded for a specific course, field, degree and institution
Sign the scholarship application form and accept the scholarship-holder obligations before departure

Exemption from the CVEC (Contribution Vie Etudiante et de Campus)
Exemption from enrolment fees for a national degree or engineering degree in public establishments under the Minister for Higher Education
Affiliation to the French social security system, with temporary free cover from a Campus France insurer for up to two months before affiliation

new_scholarship.selection_notes: Selection is run nationally, by each awarding embassy or consulate, on academic excellence; the ministry publishes no common weighting or ranking formula, and the specific criteria are set in each country's call. Campus France implements and monitors the awarded scholarship but does not select Licence-level candidates.
new_scholarship.notes: This record covers the Licence (bachelor's) level track of the Bourse du Gouvernement Français. It is deliberately NOT the France Excellence Eiffel scholarship, which is already in the database as a separate master's/doctoral record; Eiffel applications come from French institutions and do not cover Licence. Licence-level French Government Scholarships are awarded by French embassies and consulates, not by the ministry in Paris through a single central call. 'Bourse du Gouvernement Français' is an umbrella status covering several categories (bourses d'études, bourses de stage, bourses de séjour scientifique de haut niveau); this record covers the bourse d'études at Licence level.

programme_detail_official.application_cycle: Annual cycle; each French embassy or consulate abroad publishes its own call and deadline for the academic year it is awarding. No single central application window exists.
programme_detail_official.deadline_central_display: No central deadline. The ministry states: "Quel que soit leur pays de résidence, les candidats doivent donc, avant leur départ et suffisamment à l'avance, s'adresser directement à ces services situés dans leurs pays d'origine afin d'obtenir toutes les informations sur ces bourses : conditions d'attribution, calendrier de sélection, dossiers à constituer." Deadlines therefore close per country, set by the awarding embassy or consulate.
programme_detail_official.deadline_note: There is deliberately no central deadline. The Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs states that the majority of these scholarships are awarded by the cultural cooperation services of French embassies and consulates abroad, and that candidates must contact those services in their country of origin to obtain the attribution conditions, the selection calendar and the documents to assemble. The deadline_precision is therefore 'varies'. The only exact dates published centrally are admission dates for a Licence programme, which are a separate procedure and not the scholarship deadline.
programme_detail_official.status_note: The scheme is a standing annual programme rather than a single call with one deadline. Embassy and consulate calls open and close on their own national calendars, so the award is neither simply open nor simply closed on any single date. Verified against the ministry page last updated 5 August 2026.
programme_detail_official.funding_duration: Awarded for a fixed period tied to the programme, the course and the institution; the rate applies for the duration of the scholarship.
programme_detail_official.tuition_coverage_note: Tuition is covered only in part and only by exemption, not by payment. Campus France states that a French government scholarship holder, on presenting its scholarship or financial-support certificate, 'will be exempted from' paying the CVEC and from 'the payment of enrolment fees relating to pursuing a national degree or an engineering degree in public scientific, cultural, and professional establishments under the authority of the Minister for Higher Education' (Article R719-49 of the Education Code). Two limits are stated on the same page: the exemption does not extend to training fees ('Campus France does not cover the education fees and you are responsible for them') and Campus France does not reimburse enrolment or tuition fees already paid to the institution. fully_funded is therefore false: there are uncovered components (training fees, housing rent, most day-to-day living costs) and binding scholarship-holder obligations.
programme_detail_official.funding_label: French Government Scholarship (Bourse du Gouvernement Français) - EUR 900 per month at Licence (bachelor's) level, EUR 900 at Master's, EUR 1,850 at doctoral level; CVEC and public-sector national-degree enrolment fees exempted; holder must attend the programme, sit all exams and report to Campus France, and travel is only covered where the ministry or embassy funds it.

programme_detail_official.citizenship_residency: Open to foreign students only, excluding French nationals. Because the majority of awards are made by embassies and consulates, the accepted nationalities are defined country by country by the awarding mission; the ministry additionally reserves some specific programmes for particular nationality groups.
programme_detail_official.international_eligibility: Explicitly for international (foreign) students studying in France. The ministry describes the scheme as 'les bourses du gouvernement français' allocated 'pour des études, des stages ou des séjours linguistiques en France', awarded by the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs.
programme_detail_official.study_mode: full-time, on a programme in a French higher education institution
programme_detail_official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The study subject is decided by the awarding embassy or consulate in its country call. The ministry's own Paris-based programmes restrict subject areas by scheme, for example the France Excellence Eiffel master's and doctoral scheme is limited to science and technology (biology and health, ecological transition, mathematics and digital, engineering sciences) and humanities and social sciences (history, French language and civilisation, law and political science, economics and management).
programme_detail_official.application_method: A separate application, not automatic on admission. The scholarship is applied for directly to the French embassy or consulate (Service de coopération et d'action culturelle) in the candidate's country of residence, which sets the conditions and the selection calendar. Admission to a French programme is a separate procedure: first-year Licence applications go through the national 'Etudes en France' platform at pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr, where applications open on 1 October 2026 and close on 15 December 2026 for the entry year, with university responses before 30 April 2027.
programme_detail_official.application_route: French embassy or consulate abroad for the scholarship; national 'Etudes en France' / Parcoursup platform for admission to the Licence programme

programme_detail_official.description: The Bourse du Gouvernement Français is the umbrella status for French government scholarships awarded by the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs for study, internship and language stays in France. The majority are awarded by the cultural cooperation services of French embassies and consulates abroad rather than in Paris, so the Licence track is applied for and decided country by country. Campus France implements the awarded scholarship and publishes the official rate grid: EUR 900 per month for a Licence or Master's level scholarship and EUR 1,850 per month for a doctoral one. Holders are exempted from the CVEC and from enrolment fees for national and engineering degrees in public establishments under the Minister for Higher Education, but training fees and most living costs stay with the holder, and the status carries binding attendance, examination and reporting obligations.
programme_detail_official.coverage: Covers a monthly maintenance allowance of EUR 900 at Licence level (EUR 1,850 at doctoral level), exemption from the CVEC and from public-sector national-degree enrolment fees, social security affiliation with up to two months of interim cover, and air travel only where the ministry or the awarding embassy funds it. It does not cover training fees, housing rent or most day-to-day living costs.

application_readiness_checklist: Find out whether the French embassy or consulate in your country of residence awards French Government Scholarships at Licence level at all - not every mission runs a Licence call
Contact that mission well in advance for its attribution conditions, selection calendar and document list, because the ministry publishes no common window

Apply for admission to a French Licence programme through the 'Etudes en France' platform at pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr (first-year Licence applications open 1 October and close 15 December for the entry year)
Keep the scholarship application separate from the admission application - admission does not trigger funding
Have your passport entry stamp or boarding pass ready, as Campus France will not release the first monthly allowance without proof of arrival
Register with the French social security system at etudiant-etranger.ameli.fr as soon as your enrolment is finalised
Budget for the costs the scholarship does not cover, especially training fees, housing deposit and rent
common_rejection_risks: Missing the deadline set by your own embassy, which is separate from the 'Etudes en France' admission deadline
Applying through the wrong mission - applications go to the mission for the country of residence
Assuming admission to a French university automatically produces the scholarship
Not accounting for training fees, which Campus France explicitly does not cover
Failing to send the social security certificate within three months, which suspends payment
Missing the annual reporting requests to Campus France (enrolment certificate, first-semester evaluation, June examination results)
Changing institution or course of study without prior approval from the awarding ministry service or embassy
estimated_uncovered_costs: Training fees (frais de formation), explicitly excluded by Campus France
Enrolment fees at private establishments or for programmes outside the Minister for Higher Education's remit
Housing booking fee and monthly CROUS or other residence rent
Meals, laundry and other residence ancillary costs
Day-to-day living costs beyond the EUR 900 monthly allowance
Air travel where the mission does not finance the trip
Any enrolment or tuition fee already paid directly to the institution, which Campus France does not reimburse
document_audit: Scholarship application form signed before departure
Dossier exactly as specified by your awarding embassy or consulate, in its language
Admission letter or enrolment certificate for the exact programme named in your scholarship file
Passport page with arrival stamp, or boarding pass, ready to email Campus France
Certificate of exemption from the CVEC saved from messervices.etudiant.gouv.fr
Attestation d'affiliation to the French social security system

alerts.message: There is no single global deadline. Each French embassy or consulate sets and closes its own selection calendar, so track the mission for your country rather than a central date.

Campus France publishes 'Bachelor's and Master's degree rate EUR 900' and 'Doctorate rate EUR 1,850' as the official government rate grid, so the Licence (bachelor's) level is a funded track, not master's-only.
Campus France states plainly: 'Campus France does not cover the education fees and you are responsible for them.' Confirm your programme's fee type before accepting.
The allowance stops if you do not send your enrolment certificate, social security certificate, examination results or address, or if you are unjustifiably absent from your place of study.
If your international travel was financed, you must return home when the scholarship ends unless you formally waive the return ticket.

submission_workflow: Identify the French embassy or consulate covering your country of residence and check whether it awards Licence-level French Government Scholarships
Request that mission's conditions, selection calendar and document list
Apply for admission to the French Licence programme on the 'Etudes en France' platform (first-year Licence: 1 October to 15 December for the entry year)
Submit the scholarship file to the mission by its own national deadline
After award, complete and sign the scholarship application form required by Campus France
On arrival, contact Campus France using the dedicated contact in your Pass Campus France and email proof of arrival to trigger the first allowance
Within three months, send your attestation d'affiliation to the French social security system
Through the year, respond to Campus France's enrolment certificate, first-semester evaluation and June examination-results requests

research_notes.degree_level_confirmed: Confirmed on the Campus France official study-scholarship how-to guide (updated 10 April 2026), which publishes the official French government rate grid: "Bachelor's and Master's degree rate EUR 900" and "Doctorate rate EUR 1,850". The Licence (bachelor's) level is therefore an explicitly funded track of the French Government Scholarship. Corroborated by the ministry page on diplomatie.gouv.fr, which states that most French Government Scholarships are awarded by the cultural cooperation services of embassies and consulates abroad (the channel that covers Licence) rather than by the ministry's own Paris-based programmes, which it lists as master's/doctoral (Eiffel, MOPGA) or France Excellence Major.
